extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors and obituary writers (journalists deciding which deaths qualify for editorial obituaries)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for deciding whose death merits an editorial newspaper obituary (versus a paid death notice), plus format and procedural conventions for writing obituaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Death notices vs. obituaries (proper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two distinct forms: Death notices are paid family announcements; obituaries (proper) are an editorial decision and a tribute to lives of public significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify submissions: if family pays and it's a simple announcement, run as a death notice; reserve editorial obituaries for subjects with public significance or editorial interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local newspaper paid obituaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Any local resident upon death (if family pays); death notices are briefer and sometimes published free as a 'courtesy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local papers commonly run paid notices for residents regardless of public status — editorial judgment is not required when family pays; keep notices concise and follow local policy on courtesy listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial obituaries — NYT-style assignment criteria: 'Lives long enough'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the subject’s life spans long enough to have accumulated achievements or narrative depth warranting an editorial obituary (often used as an initial filter for advance obits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial obituaries — NYT-style assignment criteria: 'Accomplished enough'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the subject’s career accomplishments and public significance; strong measurable achievements (positions, awards, influence) weigh in favor of an editorial obit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial obituaries — NYT-style assignment criteria: 'Complex enough'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate storytelling potential: lives with complexity, unusual arcs, moral ambiguity, or evolution offer richer obituary copy and are likelier to merit feature obits or advance profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public achievement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major career milestones, leadership roles, or accomplishments that affected a field or the public are key signals of newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the degree to which the subject changed opinions, practices, institutions, or culture; broad or deep influence increases obituary priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized in lifetime
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honors, awards, public offices, or other formal recognition during life are objective markers of notability for obit selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthy biography
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer subjects whose life narratives contain conflict, achievement, transformation, or notable episodes that will engage readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical witness
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical witness — connection to major events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects who participated in, witnessed, or symbolized important historical events have additional obituary value for contextual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: First / pioneering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a pioneer or 'first' (first to accomplish X, break barriers) is a clear newsworthiness factor and often justifies an obituary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural figure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists and cultural contributors who shaped tastes, movements, or produced enduring works often merit obituaries focused on their work and legacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political figure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elected officials, political operatives, or other persons with political influence are standard obituary subjects due to public interest in governance and policy impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business titan
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business leaders who shaped industries, companies, or markets are newsworthy for obituaries, especially where economic impact or public reach is large.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports legend
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Athletes and sports figures with significant achievement, records, or cultural impact are typical obituary subjects for sports coverage and wider pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientist / inventor
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals whose research or inventions had measurable effects on technology, health, or knowledge are candidate obituary subjects; explain their contributions clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activist / reformer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders of social movements or reformers whose work changed laws, institutions, or social norms generally merit obituaries that contextualize their causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survivor of historic event
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People whose lives are linked to significant historical events (e.g., war veterans, disaster survivors) can be obit subjects both for personal narrative and historical testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local notable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local figures with community impact — civic leaders, notable business owners, cultural organizers — are appropriate for local editorial obituaries even if not nationally famous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead with most significant achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Format convention: Lead with most significant achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open the obituary by stating the subject’s chief accomplishment or why they are being written about to immediately signal newsworthiness to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause of death
rubrics_metrics.description: Format convention: Cause of death (if known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cause of death when confirmed and relevant; be sensitive to family wishes and legal/ethical constraints around privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survivor list
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List immediate surviving family members (spouse, children, grandchildren) as part of the standard obituary structure, keeping names and relationships clear and concise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career arc
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the trajectory of the subject’s career — origins, turning points, peak achievements — to give readers a coherent sense of their professional life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotes / quotes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use illustrative anecdotes and quotations to humanize the subject and provide memorable details; choose pieces that illuminate character or significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family background
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant family, upbringing, and formative influences that shaped the subject’s life, but avoid unnecessary intrusion into private details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishing features
rubrics_metrics.description: Format convention: Distinguishing features (eccentricities, signature work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note idiosyncrasies, signature works, or recurring themes that make the subject distinctive and help readers remember them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain advance obits pool
rubrics_metrics.description: NYT approach: Maintains pool of advance obits for prominent figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms may keep pre-written or partially written obits for prominent people; selection for the pool depends on perceived continuing public significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update advance obits periodically
rubrics_metrics.description: NYT approach: Updated periodically while subject is alive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance obits should be reviewed and revised over time to reflect recent achievements, changing reputations, or new context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid release upon confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: NYT approach: Released within hours of confirmed death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational standard: have verified confirmation and a protocol to publish promptly once death is confirmed; balance speed with accuracy and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature obits for overlooked lives
rubrics_metrics.description: NYT approach: Smaller pool of 'feature' obits — overlooked lives, marginalized communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve resources for longer-form obituaries that recover overlooked figures or tell under-covered stories; these may be produced without the immediacy constraints of advance obits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifetime impact vs. momentary celebrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Lifetime impact versus momentary celebrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize enduring contributions and long-term impact over short-lived fame when deciding obituary priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive contribution vs. fame-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Substantive contribution as opposed to fame-only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between subjects notable for genuine contributions (ideas, works, leadership) and those notable only for fleeting celebrity; the former are stronger obituary candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Local significance in local press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the subject’s importance within their community; strong local impact can justify editorial obituaries in regional outlets even absent national fame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Did they shape an era? (historical context).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the subject’s life illustrates or influenced broader historical trends, making their obituary relevant for contextual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Biography rich enough for storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the subject’s life yields a compelling narrative with clear beats and meaningful anecdotes suitable for engaging obituary copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survivor / family willingness to share
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Survivor/family willingness to share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical consideration: having family or acquaintances willing to provide interviews, documents, or access can affect feasibility and depth of obituary reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct voice / personality
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Distinct voice or personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects with memorable personal style, quotable remarks, or distinctive public persona give obituary writers material that enhances reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inflection point in field
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: Was the subject an inflection point in their field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the person’s work marks a turning point or watershed moment in a profession, discipline, or cultural trend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting historical bias — 'Overlooked' project
rubrics_metrics.description: Belated obituaries for historically excluded groups (women, people of color, LGBTQ figures) to address bias in traditional obit criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include remedial practices that expand obituary coverage to underrepresented groups, recognizing past omissions and re-evaluating significance beyond conventional markers.
